text.title: Django + Celery Background Jobs Core Rules
text.summary: 11 testable rules grounding the django-celery methodology. Each rule pairs a binary check with sourced rationale; the run-the-checklist and skip-this-methodology gates are the leaves the decision tree always keeps reachable.

rule.statement: Tasks dispatched from a transaction MUST use transaction.on_commit (or task.delay_on_commit on Celery 5.4+). Bare .delay() inside @atomic is forbidden.
rule.rationale: .delay() can execute before the commit completes, causing 'task fired but row does not exist' incidents.

rule.statement: Every @shared_task or @app.task carries an explicit dotted `name='app.module.task'` argument; never rely on the auto-discovered name, which is derived from the module path.

rationale.source: Celery docs — task names; practitioner experience.

rule.rationale: Auto-discovered names break silently on module rename or app move; already-queued jobs deserialise against a NotRegistered task and dead-letter without an alert.

rule.statement: Every task accepts a business id (order_id, refund_id) and is idempotent under that key. The strategy is declared explicitly — idempotency_key, db_upsert, check_before_act or natural_key — and retrying with the same key is a no-op or returns the same result.

rationale.source: Celery docs; distributed-systems literature; payment-integration playbook.

rule.rationale: Celery guarantees at-least-once delivery; non-idempotent tasks double-bill, double-email or corrupt counters on retry. Naming the strategy makes the guard reviewable instead of assumed.

rule.statement: Tasks declare max_retries (≤5), retry_backoff (exponential) and retry_jitter (full) explicitly on the decorator. Never rely on Celery's silent defaults; tasks without an own policy inherit a documented project-wide default.

rationale.source: AWS Architecture Blog — exponential backoff + jitter; Celery docs.

rule.rationale: Unbounded retries pin worker slots forever on a sick downstream; full jitter avoids retry storms. The default policy differs across Celery versions, so an implicit policy is unreviewable.

rule.statement: Every task sets both soft_time_limit and time_limit. soft raises SoftTimeLimitExceeded inside the task; time_limit hard-kills the worker process. Default sizing: soft = p95 latency × 2, hard = soft + 30s.
rule.rationale: Without time limits a hung task pins a worker indefinitely; the pool starves and unrelated tasks back up behind it.

rule.statement: Tasks declare an explicit queue via `@shared_task(queue='emails')` or task_routes; workers start with `-Q <queue>`. Never run a worker on the default queue only.
rule.rationale: All-tasks-on-default mixes priorities; one slow report job starves time-sensitive email tasks sharing the pool. One queue = one SLA.

rule.statement: After max_retries the task acks to a dead-letter queue — or writes a structured failure record — carrying the original payload + last exception. The DLQ has an on-call alert that fires within minutes.

rationale.source: Internal — DLQ design canon; reliability engineering.

rule.rationale: Silent terminal failures accumulate invisibly for days; DLQ + alert gives operators one place to triage and replay.

rule.statement: Task arguments are JSON-serialisable primitives or model ids — never ORM instances or Decimals without conversion. The task re-fetches fresh state by id.
rule.rationale: Pickling ORM objects breaks across migrations and across worker versions, and a serialised instance is stale by the time the worker runs it.

rule.statement: Each Django app owns its tasks.py; cross-app effects go via the contracts module, not by importing another app's task.
rule.rationale: Cross-app task imports replicate the tight coupling decomposition was meant to fix.

rule.statement: When the Applies-If preconditions hold and no Skip-If trigger applies, walk content/04-procedure.xml end-to-end and run scripts/validate-django-celery.py before declaring the task done.

rationale.source: F-066 v3 B5.6 — mandatory run leaf.

rule.rationale: Decision-tree leaves must reference a rule id. The run leaf maps "preconditions met, all gates green" to the canonical execution path.

rule.statement: If task volume < 100/day OR no broker is set up OR job dispatch must be sub-second OR the runner is not Celery (RQ, Dramatiq, Huey, Airflow, Prefect), skip this methodology.
rule.rationale: Celery overhead is wasted at low volume, unsuitable for tight-latency dispatch, and the conventions here do not transfer to a different runner.
